What did you do? List the exact steps to reproduce, in order. From the aspergillus repo, run the package the way the acceptance-oracle contract does (scripts/CLAUDE.md: standalone, stdlib-only, bare system interpreter, no venv): PYTHONPATH=python/src python3 -c 'import aspergillus'.
What did you expect to happen? import aspergillus succeeds; aspergillus.__version__ resolves to a fallback string when no installed distribution metadata is present, so any stdlib-only oracle probe that adds src to sys.path and imports the package works under bare python3.
What actually happened? Include the exact error text or output. Import raises importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError: No package metadata was found for aspergillus. python/src/aspergillus/__init__.py line 12 runs __version__ = version('aspergillus') unconditionally at import time; its own comment asserts 'The package is always installed ... so this never falls back', which is false under the bare-python3 oracle contract. This crashes the import before any package code runs.
Which surface or component? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) python/src/aspergillus/__init__.py (import-time version('aspergillus') call)
What environment and version? (OS, app/gateway build or commit, network) aspergillus repo, main @ f033731, bare system python3 3.12 with PYTHONPATH=python/src, package not pip-installed (the reducer acceptance-oracle contract per scripts/CLAUDE.md)
Is it reproducible? (always / intermittently / once) — and how often. always
What is the impact / severity? Who is blocked and how badly? Blocks the reducer re-run acceptance gate for any derived spec whose oracle probes import the package under interpreter=python3. Concretely fails asp-d88.2 0/9 (all nine oracles crash at import before behavior is tested) and will block sibling clone-detection children asp-d88.1/.3/.4, which use the same oracle-import pattern. Fix: guard the version() call (try/except PackageNotFoundError -> fallback __version__), the standard stdlib idiom.
What activity was underway when this was found? (ODC Activity — e.g. testing, code review, normal usage, reproduction attempt) reproduction attempt
What condition or event exposed the defect? (ODC Trigger — e.g. a config change, concurrent access, a boundary/edge-case input, an unusual workload) boundary/edge-case input (package importable from source but not installed as a distribution)
Which quality/capability dimension does this affect? (ODC Impact — e.g. reliability, usability, capability, performance, security, maintainability, standards, requirements — distinct from the severity/who's-blocked question above) reliability
restatement: The aspergillus package must import cleanly from its source tree when it is not installed as a distribution. The acceptance-probe contract in scripts/CLAUDE.md runs probes with the bare system python3, with no venv and only the standard library. Under that contract, `PYTHONPATH=python/src python3 -c 'import aspergillus'` currently fails with `importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError: No package metadata was found for aspergillus`. The cause is the unconditional `__version__ = version('aspergillus')` call at import time in python/src/aspergillus/__init__.py. The requirement is that this import succeeds, and that `aspergillus.__version__` resolves to a fallback string when no installed distribution metadata is present. Any stdlib-only probe that adds python/src to sys.path and imports the package must therefore work under bare python3. When the package is installed, the version must still come from the distribution metadata, so the single source of truth does not change. The source comment that says the lookup 'never falls back' is false, and it must not stay in the file.

restatement_clauses.text: From the aspergillus repo, with bare system python3, no venv, the package not pip-installed, and no aspergillus distribution metadata findable, `PYTHONPATH=python/src python3 -c 'import aspergillus'` succeeds (exit 0) and does not raise importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError.
In that same no-metadata environment, aspergillus.__version__ resolves to a fallback string (a non-empty str).
A stdlib-only probe run under bare python3 that adds python/src to sys.path (without PYTHONPATH) and imports aspergillus works: the import succeeds and __version__ is a string.
When aspergillus is installed (the python/ uv project environment), aspergillus.__version__ still equals importlib.metadata.version('aspergillus').
python/src/aspergillus/__init__.py no longer carries the false comment claim that the version lookup 'never falls back'.

goal: Importing aspergillus from source under bare python3, with no installed distribution, succeeds and gives a fallback __version__ string. The installed version still comes from the package metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Running the package the way the acceptance probes do — plain system python3 with python/src on PYTHONPATH and no installed copy of aspergillus — imports the package without error. The check also confirms that no installed copy of aspergillus was visible, so the missing-install case was really tried.
In the same uninstalled setup, the package reports a version value that is a non-empty piece of text.

A plain python3 program that uses only the standard library puts python/src on its own import search list, without PYTHONPATH, and imports the package. The import succeeds, and the program sees a text version value.
Inside the project's installed environment (uv run in python/), the version the package reports is exactly the version recorded in its install information.
The package's main file no longer says that the version lookup never falls back.
